**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Adopt cross-window proxy tabs before grouping**

When a proxy is dragged from another browser window onto this stack chip, `getDraggedTab()` returns a tab owned by the source window, but this handler stops the native drop path and later passes that foreign tab directly to `group.addTabs()`. Unlike the stack-bar drop path below, it never calls the destination browser's `adoptTab()`, so the tab cannot be correctly registered and transferred into the destination window. Adopt each foreign tab before adding it to the group, then operate on the adopted tab.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve every tab in a multiselected proxy drag**

When the proxied tab is part of a native multiselection, `startTabDrag()` places all selected tabs in the transfer, but this custom drop path reads only item 0 and then prevents the native handler from running. Dropping that proxy into the bar or back onto the strip therefore moves or adopts only the first tab while the rest of the dragged selection remains in the source position/window. Either process every native tab item in the transfer or explicitly initiate a single-tab drag for proxies.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Recover native drag state when dragend is lost**

When a drop synchronously removes the source proxy—for example, moving it into another stack or adopting it into another window—Gecko can omit the terminal `dragend`; the existing split-view drag recovery code explicitly handles this case. Here both `handle_dragend()` and the custom `PROXY_DRAG_END_EVENT` are invoked only from the proxy's own `onDragEnd`, so if that event is absent the native `_dragData` cleanup never runs and `tabDragActive` remains true, suppressing future active-stack synchronization. Schedule terminal recovery independently from the drop path rather than making the fallback conditional on receiving `dragend`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
